description:
Why The Battle of Midway Was NOT Bad Luck

At 10:22 a.m. on June 4, 1942, American dive bombers fell out of the clouds above the Japanese carrier Kaga. Within six minutes, three of the carriers that had attacked Pearl Harbor were burning. For decades this was told as five minutes of bad luck.
So was it luck at all?

In this animated documentary we follow Admiral Yamamoto's trap from the planning table to the map of the Pacific, then go down into a basement at Pearl Harbor where Commander Joseph Rochefort and Station Hypo were reading the Japanese naval code.

We look at the American carriers that were not in port on December 7, 1941, the plan to bait them out at Midway, the mystery target called AF, the fake message about Midway's broken water plant, and the Tokyo report that gave the answer away — and why four Japanese carriers against three American ones should not have been close.

The trap was reversed long before the bombs fell.

⏱ Chapters
{{CHAPTERS}}

Was Midway won in the air at 10:22 — or in a basement in May? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe for more history told from both sides.

In memory of the sailors and airmen of both navies who died at Midway.

All scenes are animated illustrations, not archival footage.
